_comment: All tunables live here so you never have to touch source code. Edit, save, restart the bot.

jupiter._comment: Jupiter's public Swap API for actually executing buys/sells. These URLs could NOT be verified live from this sandbox (no network egress here) - Jupiter has moved/renamed this endpoint before (quote-api.jup.ag -> lite-api.jup.ag among others). If swaps start failing with connection errors, check https://dev.jup.ag for the current endpoint and update here - one place, no code changes needed.

trading._comment: Master switch. MUST be flipped to true by hand once you have verified the filter logic yourself. See NON-NEGOTIABLES in README.md. Position sizing is risk-based (from stop-loss distance), not a flat SOL amount - set totalCapitalSol to your real trading bankroll. riskPercentPerTrade is your dial (0.5-1% per the strategy spec); there is ALSO a non-overridable hard cap (1% of capital) enforced in src/trading/sizing.ts that no config value can loosen - in practice that hard cap is what actually sizes most trades, see the comment there. paperTrading is a SECOND, independent safety net: even after enabled=true, real money is only ever at risk once paperTrading is ALSO set to false - until then every buy/sell is a simulated fill against real Jupiter prices, logged to logging.paperTradesFile instead of tradesFile. No wallet is required while paperTrading is true.
trading._priorityFeeComment: Priority fee (lamports) attached to swap transactions, asymmetric ON PURPOSE. A SELL that fails to land leaves you holding a position that is actively losing value - real money out the door - and sells are exactly when contention spikes, because everyone is trying to exit the same token at once. A BUY that fails to land just leaves you with no position: an opportunity cost, not a loss. Paying for buy priority also buys a speed edge this strategy does not use (see the standing 'do not compete on execution speed' decision - the filters need seconds of data, so this bot was never in the first-block race), and it would be spent on every entry attempt including the ones that would have landed anyway. buyPriorityFeeLamports is therefore 0, but the key exists so it can be tuned without a code change. 100000 lamports = 0.0001 SOL. Nothing here fires while paperTrading is true - no real transaction is ever built.

filters._comment: A token must satisfy ALL of these to PASS. Any failed rule => SKIP with a reason.

polling._walletActivitySampleSizeComment: How many recent signatures are pulled per token to count unique wallets and transactions. Each one is a getTransaction call, so this value IS the bot's RPC bill: measured 2026-09-10, getTransaction was 73% of all calls at 31,876 calls/hour with this set to 100. Helius confirmed all five methods in use cost 1 credit each, so that is ~23M credits/month against a 10M Developer plan - exhausted in ~13 days. Lowered 100 -> 20 on 2026-09-10 against that MEASURED rate, not an inferred one. This is the largest single lever on credit burn; no realistic schedule window comes close (a 14-hour day still leaves ~13.4M/month). It costs activity-metric resolution on tokens that reach the activity check at all - and note most tokens fail an earlier check and never reach it.
polling._concurrencyComment: Detected tokens are processed through a bounded queue instead of all at once. Every token previously fired its full ~110-call metrics pipeline in parallel with every other, which is what produced the HTTP 429s and 20s collection times. maxConcurrentTokens is how many are worked on at a time; maxQueuedTokens caps the backlog, and the OLDEST waiting token is dropped past that (a stale launch is worth less than a fresh one). Raise maxConcurrentTokens only if your RPC provider's rate limit has headroom.

delayProbe._comment: MEASUREMENT ONLY - has zero effect on any PASS/SKIP or trading decision. The bot evaluates a token a few hundred ms after launch, when it structurally cannot yet have minUniqueWallets/minTransactionCount - nobody has had time to trade it. Rather than guess a better evaluation delay, this re-collects metrics for the same token at each age below and writes them to logs/delay-probe.jsonl, so the right delay can be read off real data later. It runs on its OWN bounded queue so measurement can never delay a live decision or reintroduce rate-limiting. sampleRate is the fraction of detected tokens probed: measuring EVERY token needs ~22 RPC calls/second, which exceeds the plan's rate limit and collapses into 429 retries and timeouts. Probing a random subset keeps every observation fully accurate (uniqueWalletCount and transactionCount are never approximated) and simply covers fewer tokens - the right trade when the goal is picking a delay from a representative sample rather than auditing every launch. Raise it if your RPC plan has headroom. LOWERED 0.3 -> 0.08 on 2026-09-09: the first real run showed queueWaitMs medians of 10-31 MINUTES against a nominal 30s delay, because at maxConcurrentProbes:2 each job takes ~20s to time out and the queue simply cannot drain. Only 29% of observations (128/435) produced a usable reading. Fewer, cleaner observations beat many useless ones - a 30s observation actually taken 40 minutes late is not a 30s observation. EXTENDED 2026-09-09: added 1800s (30min) and 7200s (2h). At 30/120/300s the unique-wallet count plateaus at a median of 4 and a max of 10 across ALL three delays - the curve is flat, so no delay in that range gets a token near minUniqueWallets:20. The ladder has to reach further before a delay can be picked from evidence rather than guessed. Set enabled=false to switch it off. DISABLED 2026-09-09 23:20: its question is answered. 4,100 observations across 30s/120s/300s/1800s/7200s show unique wallets flat at a median of 2 at EVERY delay, and 0 of 128 evaluable observations clear the filters at any of them - waiting longer does not help, and no further sampling will change that. It was still spending RPC calls re-measuring a settled question while the live path was returning 429s on every metric. Re-enable only to re-test the delay hypothesis against a genuinely different market regime.

schedule._comment: ENABLED 2026-09-10 to cut credit use, on measured data (APPROVALS item 13). OFF 07:00-11:59 UTC, ON 12:00-07:00 - a 19-hour window crossing midnight. Those five are the five quietest MEASURED hours in npm run histogram (700-863 detections/h against a 1,677/h peak). Every hour with insufficient observation stays ON: 01-06 and 20-21 all fall inside the active window, because an hour switched off on no evidence becomes permanently unobservable. Burn scales with detections at ~10.7 calls each, measured against logs/rpc-meter.jsonl, so this removes 20.8% of the clock but only 15.3% of the burn - the saving is NOT hours x average rate. Projected 6.92-7.65M/month against the 10M plan, 23-31% headroom. Set enabled=false to revert; the meter will show within a day whether the projection held.

creditBudget._comment: Credit circuit breaker. The meter measures burn; this is what acts on it. Tristan ran out of Helius credits once with no warning, and nothing prevented a repeat. Budgets are in CREDITS, not calls - DAS methods bill at 10 credits each, so a call-based budget would have been 15% wrong the moment one went live. Defaults are derived from the 10M/month Developer plan with 10% headroom (9M/month), and the daily figure is that spread over the longest month. Measured burn on 2026-09-11 was 9,891 credits/h = ~237k/day, so 290k/day sits above the observed rate - it is a ceiling, not a target. There is deliberately NO unlimited setting: a zero, negative, missing or infinite budget is rejected at startup. Turn it off explicitly with enabled:false instead. At the limit, detection STOPS and every skipped token is recorded as "credit-halt" with decision NOT_EVALUATED - same precedent as outside-schedule, so a halt and a quiet night never look the same in the logs.
creditBudget._warnFractionComment: Warn loudly once either budget passes this fraction. Detection continues; the warning says it will stop at the limit.

supervisor._comment: NIGHT-PROMPT-V5 Project 1 (2026-09-12). The bot writes heartbeatFile every heartbeatWriteIntervalMs with the last websocket message and last detection times. A SEPARATE process (npm run supervisor) reads it and, during schedule ON hours only, restarts the bot when the websocket has been silent for wsSilenceWindowMs - after the 2026-09-12 outage where the watcher's own health timer was cleared by the stop() that then hung, leaving the process up and blind for seven hours. The supervisor opens no network connection and spends zero credits. Set enabled=false to have the supervisor exit immediately; the heartbeat is written regardless because the Dashboard reads it.

holderData._comment: How topHolderPercent and devWalletPercent are fetched. DIAGNOSED 2026-09-10 from evidence, and the stated cause was wrong: getTokenLargestAccounts DOES support Token-2022 (it succeeds on the very same mints once they are ~2 minutes old). It fails at DETECTION time because the largest-accounts INDEX has not been built yet - in the decision log the metric succeeded at a median detection-to-decision latency of 161,508ms and failed at 204ms, an 800x split, while getAccountInfo on the same mint succeeded 98% of the time. Raced head to head on 6 fresh mints at 30ms-2.5s: getTokenLargestAccounts failed 6/6, DAS getTokenAccounts succeeded 6/6. So routing is by AGE, not by token program - a legacy mint at 200ms would hit the same unbuilt index. DAS costs 10 credits against 1 (confirmed on Helius's pricing page), so it is used ONLY for tokens young enough that the cheap call would fail AND only after every cheap filter has already passed - measured, that is ~11% of tokens. One DAS call serves BOTH metrics because the response carries owner and amount per account, so it is 10 credits per surviving token, not 20. Measured added cost: ~1,323 credits/hour. DISABLED 2026-09-10 after MEASUREMENT: predicted 1,323 credits/h, measured 2,790/h over 20 minutes, which exceeds the 2,000/h gate. The code stays in place and tested; allowDas is the switch. See APPROVALS item 16 - this needs Tristan's decision, not a quiet re-enable.

rugChecks._comment: Rug checks 3 and 4 (src/data/rugChecks.ts). LP burn status is read for Raydium pools from the LP mint supply; Pump.fun tokens are recorded not-applicable, never safe. Bundle detection fetches the launch slot's transactions on the pool (1 getSignaturesForAddress + 1 getTransaction per launch-slot signature) and counts distinct buyer wallets other than the creator. It runs ONLY for tokens that passed every cheap check - the same gate as the holder call - and bundleCreditsSpent is recorded on every token so the cost is measured. maxLaunchSlotSignatures bounds the fetch; if the launch slot lies beyond that window the result is unknown, not a floor. Neither metric feeds a filter yet: no threshold exists for them (recorded, not enforced). Measured live 2026-09-11: 1 credit when the launch slot is clean, 1+N when it is not.

paperExecution._comment: MEASUREMENT ONLY - records what a position WOULD have done. There is no order path: no wallet, no signing, no transaction building. trading.enabled is irrelevant here because there is nothing to enable. Costs ZERO additional RPC calls: entry uses liquiditySol the metrics path already fetched, and tracking consumes liquidity readings the watchlist already takes. A dedicated poll loop would have cost 720-1,200 calls/h. poolFraction is the share of the pool a paper position represents and drives the slippage model - entry is priced at REALIZABLE PROCEEDS, never the headline value, so a paper fill cannot manufacture profits that could not exist. includeRejected: true opens positions for tokens the LIVE filters rejected as well as passed - that comparison is the whole point, because a 0% pass rate is unreadable until you know what the rejects did. maxOpenPositions is a hard cap and every refusal is RECORDED with its reason rather than applied silently.

raisedTakeProfit._comment: APPROVALS 43, DECIDED (a) BY TRISTAN 2026-09-12, paper book only, records only. Pump.fun positions exit on whichever fires first: the pool's real SOL falling 30% below its level at entry (2 consecutive readings after a 60 s hold) or the position's value reaching +50%. The trailing value stop above stays for every other venue and for comparison. Why: under bonding-curve pricing a -50% VALUE stop cannot fire on a drain for 87.5% of entries (curve floor above 50% below 12.4 SOL raised), so it exits 10 of 92 drains; a stop on SOL raised has no floor. Walk-forward (reports/walk-forward-exit-2026-09-12.md, 561 closes split chronologically): chosen on the first half it scored -15.7% vs the current stop's -22.6% on the second (+6.9% of stake out of sample); chosen on the second half it scored -1.6% vs -23.0% on the first (+21.4%). It still loses; it is the least-losing rule the data shows. Re-read after a week of positions under it. Set enabled=false to revert every NEW position to the trailing stop (open positions keep the rule they opened under).

shadowFilters._comment: MEASUREMENT ONLY - evaluates looser threshold sets on the SAME already-fetched metrics and records what each would have decided. Changes no behaviour; the live filters still control everything. Costs ZERO additional RPC calls by construction: evaluateFilters takes thresholds as a parameter, so a shadow set is a second call on the same in-memory object, and the module is synchronous so it cannot await a fetch. Any field the live path did not fetch stays null and is recorded as UNCHECKED - it is never fetched to fill the gap. Each set overrides only the named keys of filters; everything else is inherited from the live config, so a shadow set stays honest when the live thresholds change.

sets.rationale: half the live liquidity floor - is the floor the binding constraint?
drop the wallet/transaction floors - a token seconds old structurally cannot have them
liquidity alone, everything else off - the loosest defensible set

logging._captureRpcStatusComment: Wraps fetch in the live RPC path so every HTTP response status is recorded and the FIRST 429 is reported immediately instead of at the next 10-minute meter tick. Default false because this is the one piece of custom code that sits directly in the request path of a bot that trades - it reads status ONLY, never the body (reading the body consumes the stream and the caller gets nothing), returns the original Response unmodified, and lets every rejection propagate. Without it a 429 is byte-identical to a 200 in the meter, which is how the last credit allowance drained with no warning. Override for a single run with OPIUMO_CAPTURE_RPC_STATUS=1 in .env (gitignored) rather than editing this file. See APPROVALS.md item 8.

perps._comment: Perpetuals trading via Drift Protocol. PLUMBING ONLY - there is no entry strategy wired up yet (see README). Leverage means you can lose your whole position fast, faster than spot - keep enabled=false and env=devnet until you've read the risk engine's tests and tried it with fake devnet funds first.

fundingArb._comment: Funding Rate Arbitrage strategy: long spot (assumed already held, or deposited as Drift spot collateral yourself - this bot does NOT buy the spot leg for you, see README) + short perp, equal notional, farming the funding rate. Reuses perps.* risk gate - maxLeverage below must be <= perps.maxLeverage, and market must be in perps.allowedMarkets. NOTE: Drift settles funding roughly hourly, not the 8hr cadence common on centralized exchanges - thresholds below are expressed per-hour to match Drift's actual cadence (read live from each market, not hardcoded).

outcomeTracker._comment: MEASUREMENT ONLY - never affects a PASS/SKIP or a trade. Records what each detected token BECAME (bonding-curve SOL at each checkpoint), which is the only thing that can say whether the filters are rejecting correctly. A 0% pass rate means the filters work if none of the rejects went anywhere, and means they burn money if some did - outcome data is what separates those. One checkpoint is a single getBalance call (~1/5 the cost of full metric collection), so unlike delayProbe this tracks EVERY token: winners run 1-2% and sampling at 8% would observe almost none. Pending checkpoints persist to disk and replay after a restart, because 24h timers otherwise never survive - this bot restarts far more often than once a day. Set enabled=false to switch off. CAPACITY: steady-state pending is roughly (detections/min) x (longest checkpoint in min) x (number of checkpoints) - at the ~21 detections/min observed live on 2026-09-09 with a 24h horizon that is ~39,000, so the original 5,000 would have filled 80 minutes after every restart and then stopped following new tokens entirely, biasing the sample toward whatever launched just after a restart. Raised to 60,000. persistDebounceMs bounds state-file writes to one per interval instead of one per detection, because the whole map is serialised each time. SAMPLE RATE HISTORY: lowered 1 -> 0.3 on 2026-09-10 on the belief that the live path was rate-limited, then RESTORED to 1 the same day once the Helius dashboard showed the real cause was credit exhaustion, not throttling. The 0.3 sample bought nothing against that cause and cost 70% of the outcome data - and outcome data is the only thing that can say whether a 0% filter pass rate means the filters work or that they are burning money. Restored alongside an upgrade to the Helius Developer plan (10M credits/mo). Lower it again only against a MEASURED burn rate from logs/rpc-meter.jsonl, never against an inferred one.

watchlist._comment: Keeps tokens under observation across their life instead of judging them once, a few hundred ms after detection. Real data from 2026-09-09: of 1,236 tracked tokens exactly 3 became worth buying, and both winners examined closely started BELOW filters.minLiquiditySol and grew past it later (0.278 -> 4.348 SOL; 1.429 -> 7.39 SOL). They were rejected for being new, not for being bad. Waiting longer before the single check does not fix it either - that was tested out to 2h and the activity curve is flat. TWO TIERS, because the calls cost wildly different amounts: a liquidity reading is ONE getBalance; a full metrics evaluation is ~110 calls (walletActivitySampleSize 100 = ~91% of all RPC traffic per the latency audit). So liquidity is polled cheaply and only tokens whose liquidity actually moves earn the expensive evaluation. maxChecksPerTick is a HARD ceiling - this bot already returns 429s on a free tier, and work that does not fit waits for the next tick and is recorded, never silently dropped. A PASS goes to the same SpotTradingEngine.onFilterPass the live path uses, which still refuses everything unless trading.enabled is true - this adds no new route to a buy, only a new moment at which one is offered. In memory only: a restart empties it, which is bounded because entries age out after maxAgeMs anyway. Set enabled=false to switch off. LOWERED maxChecksPerTick 12 -> 6 on 2026-09-10: 48 RPC calls/min -> 24, because the bot was returning 429s on every metric read. Nothing about the decision rules changed - overflow still WAITS for the next tick and is recorded as skipped-budget, so this costs check frequency, never coverage. Raise it back once the RPC ceiling is understood.
